gloss: to be married to; to live together as husband and wife

definitions.gloss: to be married to; to share one's life with as a spouse
definitions.explanation: To live together as a married couple over a long period. The partner is marked with と. Slightly literary in tone and most often used of long marriages, as in {長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{添|そ}った{妻|つま} (the wife he had been married to for many years).

examples.japanese: {五十年|ごじゅうねん}{連|つ}れ{添|そ}った{夫婦|ふうふ}だ。
examples.english: They are a couple who have been married for fifty years.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{添|そ}った{妻|つま}を{亡|な}くした。
examples.english: He lost the wife he had been married to for many years.

examples.japanese: {苦労|くろう}を{分|わ}け{合|あ}いながら{連|つ}れ{添|そ}ってきた{二人|ふたり}の{絆|きずな}は{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: The bond between the two, who have lived together as a couple through hardship, is strong.

notes:
{連|つ}れる (to take along) + {添|そ}う (to be at someone's side). Intransitive: the spouse takes と, never を.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{添|そ}う: to be married for many years
- {連|つ}れ{添|そ}った{妻|つま}／{夫|おっと}: the wife/husband one has shared life with
- {添|そ}い{遂|と}げる: to stay together to the end (a near-synonym often used in the same contexts)

USAGE:
Mostly appears in the past or perfect form ({連|つ}れ{添|そ}った、{連|つ}れ{添|そ}ってきた) when looking back on a marriage. It is rarely used of a new couple, and never of dating.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {連|つ}れ{合|あ}う: to go along together — older and broader; its derived noun {連|つ}れ{合|あ}い (spouse) is the common word
- {結婚|けっこん}する: to marry — the everyday verb for the event of marrying, not the years that follow
